name: Lagbaja
current_role: Masked Afrobeat musician (stage name of Bisade Ologunde); founder of the Motherland live-music venue, Ikeja, Lagos
profile: Lagbaja is the stage persona of Nigerian saxophonist, singer and percussionist Bisade Ologunde (b. 1960, Lagos), who has performed behind a mask since the early 1990s, blending Afrobeat, highlife, jazz and Yoruba percussion. Debut album 1993; breakthrough 'We Before Me' (2000). His wealth comes from music and live events.
interesting_fact: The name Lagbaja is Yoruba for 'nobody in particular' (a John Doe); the mask is meant to represent the faceless common man in Africa, and he has said several people have played the role.
deep_cut_fact: Before music fame he studied Education/Biology at Obafemi Awolowo University, worked as a Kwara State civil servant, taught himself saxophone, and in March 1997 opened Motherland in Ikeja, modelled on a traditional African village square, for monthly concerts.
notes: The $300M figure comes from Wikidata and looks doubtful for a musician; treat it with caution. His official site (lagbaja.com) is listed as a dead link on Wikipedia, and I found no verified contact. Best route is probably the Motherland venue in Ikeja or his band management. Not an energy or data-center figure.

name: Liu Lirong
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Gionee (Shenzhen Gionee Communication Equipment); no current public role
profile: Liu Lirong founded the Chinese phone maker Gionee in 2002 and built it into a major domestic handset brand. The company hit a cash-flow crisis in 2018, and in December 2018 a Shenzhen court accepted a bankruptcy application against it. He has kept a very low profile since. A 2026 IT Home report, unverified, said he may be selling furniture in Indonesia.
notes: Very low profile since Gionee's 2018 bankruptcy, and press coverage of him is mostly negative (debts, gambling). Not a good outreach target. I found no published contact. Where he is now is unverified (https://www.ithome.com/0/939/207.htm). Sources: https://www.ifanr.com/1148318 (Dec 2018 court news) and https://www.jiemian.com/article/2643335.html.

name: Tang Yong
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Maccura Biotechnology Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 300463), Chengdu
profile: Tang Yong (唐勇) is chairman and a major shareholder (about 15%) of Maccura Biotechnology, an in-vitro diagnostics maker founded in Chengdu in 1994. Maccura started as a distributor of diagnostic products and moved into its own R&D and manufacturing. It listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board in 2015.
interesting_fact: Maccura started out as a distributor and later turned itself into a manufacturer through its own R&D. It is now one of China's leading domestic IVD suppliers.
notes: Low public profile, and I found little personal biography. The ir_email is the securities department address given in Maccura's 2025 sustainability report. The board secretary is Shi Wei. The common name has many namesakes (doctors, professors). Chairman role per https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/2144728819582214.

name: Liu Zhixiong
current_role: Founder and Chairman, 3NOD Group (Shenzhen; audio and consumer electronics)
profile: Liu Zhixiong (刘志雄), from Chaozhou, Guangdong, left school at 17 and came to Shenzhen in 1989. He worked his way up in mould factories, then in 1995 founded a mould-processing shop that became 3NOD, a maker of multimedia speakers and audio equipment. At one point 3NOD produced roughly a tenth of the world's PC speakers. He still chairs the group.
interesting_fact: On 17 August 2007, 3NOD listed on the Korea Exchange. It was reported as the first foreign (and first Chinese) company to list on the Korean market, and Liu was named a 2007 Korean securities market figure of the year.
deep_cut_fact: His first job in Shenzhen came from his calligraphy: neat handwriting got him a clerical post at a Japanese-Hong Kong joint venture. He then trained as an unpaid apprentice in a mould workshop and rose to manager before founding Xunhongda (迅鸿达), the predecessor of 3NOD, in August 1995.
notes: Founded the Shenzhen alumni association of Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business (CKGSB). The company site 3nod.com.cn returned an error when I checked, and I found no published press email. 36Kr lists a different legal representative (Liu Zhijian) for the operating entity, but the chairman role is confirmed (https://uk.marketscreener.com/insider/ZHIXIONG-LIU-A0ICG9/).

name: Keith Black
current_role: CEO and co-owner, Regatta Group (Regatta, Craghoppers, Dare2b, Regatta Professional), Manchester
profile: Keith Black runs the family-owned Regatta Group, one of the UK's largest outdoor-clothing businesses, headquartered at Risol House in Urmston, Manchester. His father Lionel bought the small wholesaler Risol Products in 1977. Keith took over in 1981 and built the Regatta brand, later adding Craghoppers and launching Dare2b in 2000. He co-owns the group with his sister Joanne.
interesting_fact: Regatta won the Queen's Award for Enterprise in International Trade in both 2012 and 2013, and its Regatta jacket won a Which? award for best waterproof jacket in 1987.
deep_cut_fact: The brand name came about by chance. In 1982 Keith bought a cancelled order of jackets printed with a sailing boat and the word 'Regatta', and the name stuck. Risol formally became Regatta in the mid-1990s.
notes: Private, family-owned company, and Keith rarely gives interviews. I found no published press email for Regatta. Ignore the pattern-based email formats on lead-gen sites. Best route is the company's head office or website contact channels.

name: Ruan Renyi
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2015-2016 (with Ruan Shouguo) with wealth from a rail-transit-systems business named 'Dinghan'. I could not confirm which company this is. Beijing Dinghan Technology (SZSE: 300011) is controlled by Gu Qingwei, and no Ruan family member appears among its main shareholders.
notes: Identity unresolved. Do not assume a link to Beijing Dinghan Technology (shareholders per https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1818824729022593). Needs Chinese corporate-registry research on 阮仁义 before any outreach.

name: Pan Jiding
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2006-2007 as founder or owner of Guotai Hengsheng Investment (国泰恒生投资), with interests in real estate and railways. Web searches turned up no other public information on 盘继顶 or the company.
notes: Very obscure, and he has not appeared on rich lists since 2007. I could not confirm identity, current status or contacts.

name: David B Blundin
current_role: Managing Partner, Link Ventures (Kendall Square, Cambridge MA); Chairman, EverQuote (NASDAQ: EVER); co-host of the Moonshots podcast
profile: Dave Blundin is an MIT-trained serial entrepreneur and investor who has co-founded about 23 companies. They include DataSage (sold to Vignette), Vestmark (wealth-management software), the Cogo Labs incubator, and EverQuote, which he has chaired since 2008. He now runs Link Ventures, an AI-focused fund backing MIT and Harvard founders, and teaches MIT's 'AI for Impact: Venture Studio' course.
interesting_fact: He co-hosts Peter Diamandis's Moonshots podcast and is on the XPRIZE Innovation Board. He has said he had been waiting for today's AI platform shift since he was 14.
deep_cut_fact: He studied AI at MIT starting in 1984, researching neural networks at the AI lab. He says he was quantizing neural networks as early as 1992, long before today's low-bit LLM inference. He has also discussed meeting Jeff Bezos and building personalization at Amazon in DataSage's early days.
notes: Highly relevant for an AI, compute and entrepreneurship podcast: he is an active podcaster and AI investor and a strong guest candidate. Best route is the Link Ventures 'Get in touch' form or the Moonshots/Diamandis team. EverQuote IR (investors.everquote.com) is a formal fallback.

name: Martin Tuchman
current_role: CEO, The Tuchman Group / Kingstone Capital V; director of FTAI Aviation and Princeton Bancorp; chair of the Tuchman Foundation
profile: Martin 'Marty' Tuchman (NJIT '62, Seton Hall MBA '68) co-founded the container lessor Interpool in 1968 and later the chassis lessor Trac Lease. Interpool listed on the NYSE in 1993 and was sold to Fortress in 2007 for about $797M. He now runs the Tuchman Group (real estate, banking, shipping) and Kingstone Capital V, sits on the FTAI Aviation board and is a large Princeton Bancorp holder.
interesting_fact: NJIT's business school, the Martin Tuchman School of Management, is named after him. As an engineer at Railway Express Agency he helped create the intermodal container and chassis standard that lets boxes move between rail, truck and ship, and it is still in use.
deep_cut_fact: At 25 he was on the Railway Express Agency team that developed the container twist lock. He got the idea for Interpool while on vacation in Bermuda, seeing containers chained to chassis, and later said of the container business: 'This isn't rocket science, it's a hole.'

public_contacts.value: See FTAI Aviation investor relations (board-member page)

notes: Longtime Princeton, NJ resident and active local philanthropist (TASK soup kitchen trustee, Seton Hall and TESU scholarships, YingHua International School). Central Jersey reports he long owned Princeton's PJ's Pancake House (https://archive.centraljersey.com/?p=684317). I could not open that article to verify it. Avoid opening with his Parkinson's philanthropy unless it is relevant. I found no direct email; best route is the Tuchman Group office or FTAI IR.

name: Michael Wright
current_role: Founder (retired) of Riviera Travel, Burton-on-Trent; private investor and philanthropist
profile: Michael Wright founded Riviera Travel in 1984. It began as cheap escorted coach tours to France and grew into the UK's largest escorted-tour operator, adding Eurostar tours and, from 2008, river cruises on its own ships. He and his wife Claire sold control to Phoenix Equity Partners in 2014 (about £130M to them), and Riviera was later sold on to Silverfleet for about £250M. He is now retired and manages his own investments, including stakes in Phoenix funds.
interesting_fact: By 2014 Riviera served 110,000+ customers a year on about £130M turnover. Wright chose a private-equity buyer over larger trade rivals partly to protect his staff.
deep_cut_fact: After hating a bank job his mother suggested, he went to work at a campsite in France. There he sold iced, nicely garnished melons on the beach ('crinkle cut lemons... a 600% markup') and built up a fleet of about 120 rental caravans before switching to coach tours.
notes: Retired and private, with no published personal contact. A common name, so match him by Riviera Travel. He has said his only plan is 'to be happy'. Low fit for an energy or data-center podcast, but a good founder story.

name: Sam Darwish
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, IHS Holding Ltd (IHS Towers; NYSE: IHS)
profile: Sam Darwish grew up in Beirut during the civil war and studied at AUB. After working at MCI and helping launch Lebanon's first mobile network at Libancell, he became deputy MD of Motophone, Nigeria's first GSM operator, in 1998. He founded IHS Towers in Lagos in 2001 and built it into one of the world's largest independent tower companies (tens of thousands of sites in Africa and Latin America). IHS listed on the NYSE in 2021.
interesting_fact: IHS began in Lagos in 2001 as Nigeria opened up its telecoms sector, and it grew into one of the largest independent multinational tower operators. In early 2026 MTN proposed buying the remaining stake, valuing IHS at about $6.2B.
deep_cut_fact: Before IHS he helped set up Lebanon's first mobile network at Libancell (now Touch). He is also a trustee of the George & Barbara Bush Foundation and has helped run tech-entrepreneur incubator programmes in Lagos.
notes: Strong fit: telecom tower infrastructure, power-intensive sites in emerging markets, and a digital-infrastructure angle. Check the status of the 2026 MTN buyout, since it may change his role. A Brazil Journal profile calls him 'the Indiana Jones of IHS Towers'. The IHS sites blocked automated access, so I could not verify an IR or press email. The contact_form URL is the standard IR contact path and is unverified.

name: Challa Rajendra Prasad
current_role: Executive Chairman, CCL Products (India) Ltd (Continental Coffee)
profile: Challa Rajendra Prasad is the promoter and executive chairman of CCL Products (India), based in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh. CCL started instant-coffee manufacturing in 1994 and calls itself the world's largest exporter of instant coffee and a leading private-label maker. It sells in 110+ countries and also has its own consumer brand, Continental Coffee.
interesting_fact: CCL says it offers more than 1,000 coffee blends and is the largest exporter of instant coffee worldwide. Its registered office is in the small town of Duggirala in Guntur district, not a metro.
notes: His re-appointment as director and executive chairman is shown in CCL's investor filings. Low media profile. The company-secretary address is the formal route. I ran out of web-search budget before finding a sourced deep-cut fact.

name: Yogarathinam Nadar
profile: S. Yogarathinam Nadar, from Panika Nadar Kudiyiruppu village near Tuticorin, founded Saravana Stores in 1969 with his brothers. It started as 'Shanmugam Stores', a small vessels shop, and opened its first T. Nagar, Chennai complex in 1977. It grew into what is described as Tamil Nadu's largest family-owned retail chain. The family business has since split into several separately run Saravana-branded chains.
interesting_fact: The family's group launched its own 100% milk ice-cream brand, Jamaai, in 2004 with a factory at Padappai.
deep_cut_fact: The retail empire began as Shanmugam Stores, a small shop selling vessels and named after the founders' father Shanmuga Sundaram Nadar, before becoming Saravana Stores in T. Nagar in 1977.
notes: Wikipedia cites a 2015 news headline about the loss of 'Annachi' that may refer to his death. I could not confirm whether he is alive, so verify before any outreach. The business is now run by other family members. I found no published contact.
